title: Introduce capability-scoped API keys for API and MCP access
description:
Problem: a single configured API key can satisfy multiple permission classes, allowing one credential to act as read-only, source-sensitive, write, or administrator access depending on the endpoint being evaluated.

Desired outcome: API keys resolve to explicit capabilities instead of implicitly satisfying every policy. Preserve a deliberate compatibility mode only when an operator explicitly chooses a superuser-style key.

Scope:
- Map each presented key to a principal and explicit capabilities such as read, source-read, write, and admin.
- Deny operations outside the key capability set.
- Document rotation and compatibility behavior without exposing key material.
- Add a security matrix covering anonymous, read-only, source-read, write, admin, and auth-disabled modes.
- Out of scope: external identity-provider redesign.

Acceptance criteria:
- Read-only keys cannot invoke write operations.
- Write keys cannot manage users or security settings without admin capability.
- Source-sensitive reads require an explicit source-read capability.
- Tests prove the full capability matrix and explicit compatibility mode behavior.
- Unauthorized responses do not reveal whether a higher-privilege capability exists.

Validation:
- Run focused authorization and MCP tests.
- Run the security regression matrix.
- Run Test-TaskRecords.ps1 after task metadata changes.
